scope: Five pivotal Mara/Nia scenes: narrative-first responsive frames and an intimate scene mix, using every existing exact-word performance and painting.

scenes.label: Mara · from the shard

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: I signed the coolant dump. Ward Nine. Three hundred on the night shift. I want that sentence to stay in my mouth.

scenes.artDecision: Reuse Mara’s established recorded likeness and viewer. The complete 3:2 plate sits beside the canonical words on wide screens and follows them on phones. Neither framing nor her recorded explanation grants present-day permission or removes responsibility.

scenes.label: The recorded explanation · Mara

dialogue.speaker: Mara
dialogue.text: Helion told me the dump was a flush, not a kill. I signed because the night shift was already in the building and I thought the tower would move them. They did not move them.

scenes.label: Before the crossing · Nia

dialogue.speaker: Nia Pell
dialogue.text: You promised a witness. I promised nothing to a transmitter. I need care, a room they don't own, and a say in which words leave it. Can you do those separately?

scenes.artDecision: Reuse Nia’s established pre-transfer or arrival composition at its actual chronological scene. The complete plate accompanies her canonical words, without depicting recording, a private address, treatment, gratitude or permission not earned by the choices.

voiceDecision: Every exact spoken part, actor, order and delivery remains unchanged. Canonical prose renders once; emphasis derives only from actually revealed, bound quotation ranges. No narration, player text, duplicate quotation panel or runtime speech synthesis is added.
audioDecision: Use the existing reading score for Mara and quiet score for Nia. Pre-transfer Nia remains in Glass Chapel clinic ambience; arrival retains the private witness-room bed. An intimate bus multiplier reduces music to 55% and ambience to 75% of their selected levels, in addition to existing speech ducking. Voices and effects retain their own controls. Leaving the frame restores normal scene levels; slider restarts retain focus.
accessibilityDecision: Whole-scene and saved paragraph pacing remain. The header and goal lead; phone prose precedes the complete artwork, desktop frames it beside the prose. No forced delay, camera motion, scrolling, focus jump or automatic choice. Text-only and missing-art play remain complete.
